title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is very faint pencil and ink, so only the skeleton of the argument is legible. It opens a manuscript on 'dévissage' of ½-simplicial (semi-simplicial, i.e. face maps only) complexes that are ∂-perfect, and on their multiplicative structures.

Lemma 1 (reconstructed). Let L_* be a semi-simplicial complex of k-modules. For L_* to be a projective object (a projective ½-simplicial k-module), it suffices that:
- each L_n is a projective k-module; and
- L_* is 'flasque'.

The NB restates flasqueness as π_i(L_n)=0 for i>0 and π_0(L_n) k-projective. This reads as a homotopical acyclicity condition on certain associated chain complexes, with π_0 required to be projective; the indexing is not fully legible.

The partly legible proof:
- It passes to the associated chain complexes (the normalized or Moore complexes, via a Dold–Kan-type comparison).
- It uses the fact that a bounded-below acyclic complex of projectives splits, and is therefore isomorphic to a sum of elementary complexes.
- It concludes that L_* is isomorphic to a direct sum of standard free or projective semi-simplicial pieces.
- The NB adds that one must also account for the extra modules coming from the face structure (the absence of degeneracies). One of these is a projective module, which is why π_0 must be projective.

Corollary. For i>0, the modules Γ^i L_{*k} ⊗_k Λ^j T_{*k} (divided powers of L tensor exterior powers of T) are projective semi-simplicial modules. An interlinear addition extends this to Λ^i L ⊗ Λ^j T.

Purpose: these are the graded pieces of Koszul-type complexes Γ(L)⊗Λ(T). Their projectivity is exactly what one needs to apply non-additive functors (Dold–Puppe style) and to define determinant-like multiplicative invariants of perfect complexes. Such multiplicative structures on perfect complexes are the topic named in the archive title.

The 'next page' (an appendix on the Hirsch method from Sullivan's rational homotopy paper) is unrelated material filed in the same folder.
errors: The flatness/flasque condition is stated in two non-identical forms (π_i(L_n)=0 for i≥n vs. for i>0 with π_0 projective). The NB itself signals that the first argument was incomplete because it ignored the extra projective module in degree 0; Grothendieck corrects this on the page.

Dold–Kan does not literally apply to semi-simplicial (face-only) objects. Any comparison with chain complexes must be the weaker semi-simplicial version, and the legible text does not make this precise.

ideas.what: Criterion for a semi-simplicial k-module to be projective: degreewise projective plus a homotopical 'flasque' (acyclicity) condition
ideas.modern_name: Projective objects in semi-simplicial modules / cofibrant objects; Dold–Kan-type correspondence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold, Kan (Dold–Kan correspondence, 1958); semi-simplicial variants folklore

ideas.what: Projectivity of Γ^i L ⊗ Λ^j T (and Λ^i L ⊗ Λ^j T) for projective semi-simplicial L, T
ideas.modern_name: Non-additive derived functors (divided/exterior powers) of simplicial modules; Koszul complexes; décalage LΛ^i(L[1]) ≃ LΓ^i(L)[i]

missed.claim: Part of a project (1975–76) on multiplicative structures (determinants, λ-structures) for ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes. It is contemporaneous with Knudsen–Mumford (1976) and predates Deligne's 'Le déterminant de la cohomologie' (1987). This page only gives the technical projectivity lemma, so nothing beyond routine is visible here.
missed.quote: Cor Les Γ^i L_{*k} ⊗_k Λ^j T_{*k} (pour i > 0) sont des modules ½ simpliciaux projectifs.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest: it documents Grothendieck working on determinant or λ-ring structures of perfect complexes in a semi-simplicial setting. The page content itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine technical lemma on projectivity of semi-simplicial modules and of divided/exterior power constructions, of a kind well known from Dold–Puppe and Illusie. It is only of mild historical interest for the larger project.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 of the lemma probably reads 'Soit L_* un complexe de k-modules ½ simpliciaux' (or similar), not just 'un complexe ½ simplicial'.
'Pour que L_* soit un k-module ½ simplicial projectif' — the '½ simplicial' qualifier appears to be present.
The margin addition above the Cor reads 'et Λ^i L_{*k} ⊗ Λ^j T_{*k}', extending the corollary to exterior powers of L as well.
The next page (Appendix H, Hirsch method) is from Sullivan's rational homotopy paper, not Grothendieck's text.
